net.text: During the thirteen weeks ended September 27, 2026, net income was $10 million compared to net income of $32 million in the prior year, decreasing $22 million, or 69% year over year. The decrease was primarily driven by higher general and administrative expenses previously discussed as well as a $7 million increase in income tax expense, a $6 million loss on debt extinguishment and a $2 million revaluation of contingent liability; these increases were partially offset by our revenue growth and a $7 million gain on sale of company-owned stores this quarter.

ocf.text: Our primary sources of liquidity are our cash and cash equivalents, available borrowings under our variable funding notes (“VFN”) facility and cash generated by operating activities. As an asset-light franchisor, our primary non-operational uses of cash include capital expenditures to support technological initiatives, investments in our corporate headquarters, development of a limited number of company-owned stores and debt service. At times, we may also elect to purchase, open or divest company-owned stores, though we currently have no plans to materially increase the number of company-owned stores. In addition, we expect to use cash to repurchase shares of our Class A common stock under our share repurchase program, pay dividends and to fund future payments under the Tax Receivable Agreement, which may increase as a result of future exchanges of Common Units for shares of Class A common stock. We believe that cash provided by operating activities and existing cash and cash equivalents on hand, together with amounts available under our VFN facility, are sufficient to satisfy our anticipated cash requirements for at least the next twelve months.

capex.text: (a) Capital expenditures, comprising of purchases of property and equipment and capitalized software costs, for the thirty-nine weeks ended September 27, 2026 (Successor), for the period from January 16, to September 28, 2025 (Successor), and for the period January 1 to January 15, 2025 (Predecessor) were $7 million, $9 million and none, respectively.

Royalties.text: We primarily generate revenue from our franchise system including royalties and advertising revenue, which are a percentage of sales that are collected from franchise owners over the course of the term of the franchise agreement. Other sources of revenue include supplier program payments, technology fees, franchise fees and gift card breakage revenue.

intro.text: Jersey Mike’s Subs Inc. (the “Corporation” and, together with its consolidated subsidiaries, “Jersey Mike’s” or the “Company”) was incorporated as a Delaware corporation on February 24, 2026 for the purpose of facilitating an initial public offering (the “IPO”) and related transactions in order to carry on the business of Jersey Mike’s HoldCo, LLC (“Jersey Mike’s Holdings”) and its subsidiaries. Following the IPO and the Reorganization Transactions described below, the Corporation is a holding company whose principal asset is its equity interest in Jersey Mike’s Holdings, held directly or indirectly through wholly owned subsidiaries. As the managing member of Jersey Mike’s Holdings, the Corporation operates and controls all of the business and affairs of Jersey Mike’s Holdings and, through Jersey Mike’s Holdings and its subsidiaries, conducts the Company’s business.
